messages.author: f0d4c7c39276e09b
messages.subject: Running Time
parts:
Phil,

This is the code I'm running:


m3pl <- mirt.model("F1 = 1-45 
                   PRIOR = (1-45, a1, lnorm, 0.2, 0.2), 
                   (1-45, d, norm, 0, 1), 
                   (1-45, g, norm, -1.386294, .2)")
mt_m3pl1 <- mirt(Respostasmt2009_concluintes, 
                 model = m3pl,
                 TOL = 1e-10,
                 technical = list(NCYCLES = 1000, MAXQUAD = 40000),
                 itemtype="3PL",
                 GenRandomPars = TRUE,
                 quadpts = 20)
mt_m3pl_pars1 <- coef(mt_m3pl1 , simplify=TRUE, IRTpars=TRUE)$items

I have doubts about the time it is taking to calculate it... This sample "Respostasmt2009_concluintes" has 167,000 rows with 45 columns, and it's running in less than a minute, is this right (common)?
Also I've tried setting the NCYCLES, but it only iterates 100 times (give or take, sometimes it runs 137), why is this occurring?


Thanks a lot.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Running Time
parts:
More than likely given the size of the data set and length of the test the maximum likelihood location is extremely peaked, so the EM algorithm converges very quickly to this well defined area. Regarding why mirt is running so fast in terms of total clock time, the package it optimized in a few areas to help tackle moderately large data-sets.

Phil
